findings.title: test_mid_high_port_ceilings spawns a house on the high router's own tile (i=8 -> {20,26})
findings.detail: The 9th house (i=8) lands on x=20,y=26 — the high router's tile — so the 9th pipe is zero-span and two live nodes share one tile, contradicting the test's own 'max span 16' comment. The 17th-pipe .Router_Ports_Full assertion still holds (ports count per pipe regardless of span).
findings.recommended_fix: Skip x=20 in the house row (e.g. spawn the router at {20,27} or stagger the row) and correct the span comment.

findings.title: Tray chip -> type_idx arming has zero automated coverage (lens-guard defect class: a chip arming the wrong tier)
findings.detail: The path is generic and reads correct at review (tray_router_types yields catalog-order junction indices; the click arms rts[k]). But no test pins it: harness demos place by name (harness/demo.odin place directive), and app/ has no *_test.odin. A wrong-tier chip would ship silently.
findings.recommended_fix: Lift chip-index -> type_idx mapping into a pure proc with a unit test, or add a harness tray-click scenario asserting the placed node's tier.

findings.title: Tier-scaled placement ghost (draw_place_ghost) has zero test coverage
findings.detail: New render behaviour (ghost scales with the armed tier) is never exercised: every harness capture renders with drag={}. A wrong scale or a bad guard would ship unseen. Cosmetic, render-only.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin router_tier_scale (1.0/1.15/1.30) in a small unit test, or add a harness capture with an active placement drag.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
findings.detail: P0 100% (kind-split separation boundaries 4/3, terminal floor 2/1, mid/high port ceilings 9th/17th, tier placement, replay E10, catalog fail-fast rows — all unit-pinned; 4 new T2 captures). P1 ~80% (tray chip arming + placement ghost uncovered). Overall >=80%. Not a blocker; close the two P2 gaps to reach PASS.
findings.recommended_fix: Cover tray chip-to-type_idx arming and router_tier_scale, then the gate is PASS.

findings.title: Outer LED ring comment claims 180°/alternating geometry; code implements +4 = 90° with both rings fully populated
findings.detail: For leds=16, stride=1: the outer ring covers all 16 positions at a +4 (90°) offset, so every angle has an inner AND outer LED. The rendered concentric double ring satisfies look-book A3 'double light ring'; only the comment misdescribes the geometry.
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the comment to '+4 = 90°, both rings fully populated' (or use +8 if the alternating layout was intended).

findings.title: Ceiling-reject T2 pins the full-ceiling state, not the reject firing
findings.evidence:
# The T2 captures show the FULL-ceiling state — a 9th pipe onto the mid / 17th
# onto the high would reject .Router_Ports_Full (the reject count is pinned by
# the core unit test test_mid_high_port_ceilings; a rejected command cannot
findings.detail: Briefing asked for 'T2 of an 8-port / 16-port ceiling reject'; a rejected command cannot ride a demo action log (it latches replay_error), so the golden pins the full-ceiling state and the reject is unit-pinned. Disclosed in the PR body + demo comment — no action, documentation only.
findings.recommended_fix: None required; the substitution is documented. Optionally add an expect-reject demo directive in a later story.

findings.title: Core load validation pins the canon 4/8/16 junction ladder using a render-geometry justification
findings.detail: The ladder gate is canon-correct (GDD M3 + user ruling), but its comment justifies the check via the render's LED ring — a presentation concern reaching into core catalog validation. Design taste, not a defect; the gate itself should stay.
findings.recommended_fix: Optionally re-word the comment to lead with the canon ladder (M3/ODN-5) rather than the render geometry, or split a generic junction port_capacity > 0 check from the canon-locked ladder.

findings.title: New junction port-ladder gate validates a jint-truncated value while the placement seps use jint_strict
findings.evidence:
nt.port_capacity = jint(eo, "port_capacity", 0)
... if nt.port_capacity != 4 && nt.port_capacity != 8 && nt.port_capacity != 16 {
findings.detail: jint truncates json.Float (8.9 -> 8 passes the new gate) — the exact silent-truncation class the placement block rejects via jint_strict (the 2026-08-13 integer-only bar). Pre-existing parse for this field; the new gate inherits it.
findings.recommended_fix: Parse port_capacity with jint_strict (reject on !ok) before the ladder check, matching the placement-block precedent.

findings.title: Load-time snap-floor check multiplies two i32 tunables and can wrap on extreme-but-valid values
findings.evidence:
if b.placement.router_terminal_sep_tiles * b.tile_px < b.snap_radius {
			return {"balance.json", "placement", "router_terminal_sep_tiles * tile_px must be >= snap_radius (the E4 snap-disambiguation floor)"}
findings.detail: sep (jint_strict-bounded i32) * tile_px (>0, jint) wraps i32 on absurd retunes — the common wrap direction false-rejects (fail-safe); an accept-side bypass needs a ~65k-px tile. The PR's own topology.odin comment claims i64 discipline; the load check multiplies in i32.
findings.recommended_fix: i64(sep) * i64(tile_px) < i64(snap_radius) — one cast, matches placement_valid's convention.

findings.title: max(1,sep) zero-separation clamp in placement_valid is untested
findings.detail: Every test fixture sets Placement_Balance explicitly (determinism_test.odin:48), so the documented zero-value clamp branch never executes in any test.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a placement test with a zero-value Placement_Balance: an adjacent placement must reject via the clamp-to-1 path.

findings.title: draw_nodes type-index bounds guard (continue) is untested
findings.detail: The new defensive guard has zero coverage — no harness scenario or test produces an out-of-range node_type. Low risk, documented defensive code.
findings.recommended_fix: Accept as defensive code, or add a direct render test feeding an out-of-range type index.

findings.title: Unit tests pin placement tunables against embedded mirrors, not data/balance.json
findings.detail: A retune of data/balance.json (e.g. sep 3) leaves every unit test green — the mirrors never load the real file. The harness catalog-hash golden does catch it (all goldens reject until re-bless), so the gap is a unit-level blind spot, not a release risk.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a unit test that loads the real data/balance.json and pins the placement values equal to the embedded mirrors.
